name: The periodic table and groups 0, 1 and 7

terms.definition: A column in the periodic table; elements in a group have the same number of electrons in their outer shell and similar reactions.
terms.examiner: The group number equals the number of outer electrons (except Group 0).

terms.definition: Ordered elements by atomic weight but left gaps for undiscovered elements and swapped some pairs to fit patterns.
terms.examiner: The discovery of isotopes later explained why some pairs were out of order.

terms.definition: An element that forms positive ions when it reacts.
terms.examiner: Metals are to the left of and below the zig-zag line.

terms.definition: Group 0 elements: unreactive because their outer shell is full (stable arrangement of electrons).
terms.examiner: Boiling point increases down the group.

terms.definition: Group 1 elements: react with water to give hydrogen and a metal hydroxide; reactivity increases down the group.
terms.examiner: The outer electron is further from the nucleus, so it is lost more easily.

terms.definition: Group 7 elements: diatomic non-metals whose reactivity decreases down the group.
terms.examiner: Melting and boiling points increase down the group.

terms.definition: A more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive one from a solution of its salt.
